title: Prospective evaluation of whole-body diffusion-weighted MRI for staging patients with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
summary: Investigation of how well a specialized whole-body MRI (with diffusion imaging) detects liver lesions and recurrences in a specific type of gastrointestinal tumor (GEP-NET). The imaging results were compared with established methods (SSTR-PET/CT and liver MRI). Over a period of 12 months, patients were regularly monitored to assess the disease stage (so-called re-staging). Additionally, the study examined whether the imaging results were associated with the further course of the disease – such as overall survival or disease progression.

interventions.name: Single-arm, prospective observational study in patients with histologically confirmed GEP-NET undergoing clinically indicated SSTR-PET/CT and liver MRI. In addition, whole-body diffusion-weighted MRI is performed as part of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age: ≥18 years
- Histologically confirmed GEP-NET
- Indication for an SSTR-PET/CT and a liver MRI with hepatocyte-specific contrast agent
- Life expectancy of at least 6 months
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindication to PET/CT
- Contraindication to MRI
- Known pregnancy
